_readme: COSMETICS. The reward layer the progression tracks were queuing behind.
WHAT IS AUTHORED HERE vs WHAT IS DERIVED. Only the parts that are a joke or a
named thing in the design live in this file: the ten faction titles (08 §13 names
them exactly), the emblem each faction's card back is drawn with, and the emote
phrases. Everything visual is DERIVED from content the game already has - a card
back is the faction's colour plus its emblem, a profile frame is its crest ring, a
portrait badge is the character's own art. That is the same bargain the card
renderer already makes, and it means adding a faction gets cosmetics for free.
PER-ENTITY COSMETICS ARE NOT LISTED, THEY ARE GENERATED. There are twenty leaders
and several hundred characters, and 08 §13 asks for a title per leader ('Voice of
<Leader>') and per character ('<Character>'s #1 Fan'). Cataloguing those by hand
would be several hundred lines that say the same thing, and every one of them a
chance to name a card that does not exist. cosmetics.ts generates them from the
content index instead, so they cannot drift out of sync with the cards.
IDS ARE 'kind:scope:entity[:n]'. The kind is a slot you equip into; the entity is
what it was earned from. tests/cosmetics.test.ts checks every id a reward can
grant resolves to a real cosmetic, in both directions.

_note: 08 §13's table, verbatim. One per faction, earned at Faction Mastery rank 20.
Titles are text-only and purely cosmetic, which is why they are the one
cosmetic kind that needs no art pipeline at all.
The shape drawn on a faction's card back and inside its profile frame. The
renderer knows these ten names; adding an eleventh needs a case in
drawEmblem(), which the test enforces so a typo cannot ship a blank back.
Cosmetics that belong to no faction, leader or character - the ones handed out
by achievements (08 §9) and by achievement-point milestones. Everything else in
this file is derived from an entity that supplies its own colour and emblem;
these have nobody to inherit from, so they carry their own.
The five titles here are 08 §13's, verbatim, and §13 is where each one's source
is written down. 'kind' has to match the slot the id names, which cosmetics.ts
enforces - otherwise 'frame:award:stormfront' would resolve to a title and be
worn in the frame slot, drawing nothing.

gauntlet.name: Gauntlet Card Back
gauntlet.source: The Gauntlet — five card-back tokens, or one 12-win run

_note: One block per Hype Wave season (08 §10). A season's cosmetics are a colour, an
emblem, a title and three emote phrases - everything else about them is derived,
which is why adding a season is data rather than art. The card back also comes in
tints: same emblem, different colour, which is what 08 §10.3 means by 'card-back
tints' among the Backstage track's minor cosmetics.
Seasonal cosmetics are NOT permanently exclusive - 08 §10.3's Rerun Vault returns
them to the shop two seasons later. Nothing here is missable, which is why none of
it is announced with a countdown.

set: This is my first upload, be nice.

_note: The themed card back a Headliner Banner grants on your first ×10 pull (07 §4.1).
One per banner, and kept across the banner's reruns - a rerun is the same banner,
so it does not hand out a second copy of the same back.
08 §11's step-10 reward: a monthly rotating cosmetic. One card back per month,
chosen by the calendar month rather than by a streak - the whole point of §11 is
that there are no streaks, so which one you get depends on WHEN, never on HOW
OFTEN. Emblems are reused from the faction set on purpose: these are minor
cosmetics, and inventing twelve more shapes for them would be twelve shapes.
Twelve entries covers a year. Year two repeats, and until more are authored a
player who already owns that month's back gets nothing new from step 10 - which
checkCheckInData() reports rather than hides. That is a content problem, not a
code one, and the honest fix is more months.
Faction emote I lands at Faction Mastery rank 12, set II at rank 15, and a
leader emote at Leader Mastery 3. They join the six the battle HUD already
ships, which stay unlocked from the start - a game that starts you with no way
to say 'well played' is worse than one with no unlockables.
